analysis: Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change; no executable code, auth logic, keys or configuration is modified. The patch excerpt shows added prose around lines 453-473 describing cluster onboarding stop handling (ClusterOnboardingStopped, ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked, ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked). That excerpt is truncated, so only its description is visible; the unit text covers lines 6833-7665, which are surrounding unchanged-or-docs content. Security-relevant statements I checked against the threat model: (1) Cluster SSD prefix record encoding (lines ~7166-7330) says records are encrypted on the SSD tier, sealed with encoding in the header, bound into the load agreement, and that mismatched or foreign-encoding records are refused and deleted. This is consistent with T-041's retained cache posture (HMAC names, TTL, AES-GCM, salt scoping) and does not claim any loosening of TTL, naming or metadata. One thing worth flagging: the doc records that restored encoded rows are approximate, so a restored request can diverge from a cold prefill. That is a correctness note, not a confidentiality regression. (2) Kept-verbatim rows and pinned source records add no new at-rest metadata fields, as far as the doc describes. (3) GLM image, pair admission, paged KV and GPT-OSS sections describe fail-closed behavior (a refused load on agreement mismatch, no fallback from the encrypted data plane to raw transport, coordinator grants reject the candidate profile). No weakening of the T-008-style fail-closed encryption claims is stated. (4) The stop-count text shown in the patch describes a lifecycle control between two Macs of one owner; the authentication of the control channel is not visible in the supplied excerpt, so I cannot assess it. Remaining integration question: the actual source changes backing these docs (ClusterControlReply, the ssd prefix tier, NativeCheckpointRowCodec) are not supplied, so I did not verify that the code matches the documentation. No concrete security regression is identifiable from documentation alone.
